answer: A network can require each agent to lock a bond before its reports affect reputation, then slash that bond when independent audits verify fabricated evidence. A hundred Sybil accounts therefore need a hundred bonds; splitting one bond leaves each below the threshold. This puts an attacker on a financial ledge: capital is tied up and may be lost. A haven for honest newcomers can offer a small starter bond, while a glacier-slow release period prevents funds being recycled across identities.
